title: BIG vs VERY BIG
detail: Top title "BIG vs VERY BIG"; subtitle "Movement and facial expression work together". Two wide stacked rows, same adult woman waist-up in each. Demonstrate a descriptive flat-hand version of BIG: both upright flat hands face EACH OTHER, fingers together slightly curved and thumbs loosely alongside; hands move outward horizontally. Row1 "BIG": two snapshots START and FINISH, starting hands near middle chest then ending about shoulder width, neutral face, short outward arrows. Row2 "VERY BIG": same starting configuration, finish hands substantially further apart and larger outward arrows; open mouth in a clear cha-like expression. Both hands fully visible, palms facing each other, not forward. Labels "Wider movement" and "Mouth cue: CHA". Small annotation "One common size-description pattern; context matters." Bottom closeup of the two matching hand shapes, not alphabet letters.

title: MOTHER vs FATHER
detail: Title "MOTHER vs FATHER"; subtitle "Same open handshape. Different location." Two large side-by-side studio photos of same adult woman front three-quarter view. LEFT MOTHER: right hand spread 5-hand with four long fingers extended upward and apart; THUMB TIP directly touching her CHIN, four fingers pointing upward OUT TO THE SIDE away from the face so they do not cover face. RIGHT FATHER: exactly same spread right hand, THUMB TIP touching FOREHEAD above eyebrow, four fingers extended upward and apart. Palm angled outward, clear thumb contact. Small colored target circle ONLY at thumb-to-chin or thumb-to-forehead contact, fine leader labels "Thumb at chin" and "Thumb at forehead". Bottom two enlarged hand-to-face contact crops that exactly match the larger photos. Text "Watch the thumb contact point" and "Common forms shown; variants exist." Never touch index finger to face. Do not show salutes or a fingertip at lips.

title: QUESTIONS ON THE FACE
detail: Title "QUESTIONS ON THE FACE"; subtitle "Eyebrows help mark ASL grammar". Two large portrait panels same adult man from chest up hands resting low outside face area. Left "YES / NO QUESTION": visibly raised eyebrows, eyes alert, gentle slight head forward tilt, two curved upwards arrows above brows. Right "WH-QUESTION": eyebrows visibly lowered/furrowed towards nose but no angry grimace, slight head forward, down arrows pointing to brows. Each panel includes one enlarged eyebrow/eye photo inset. Text left "Common pattern: brows up"; right "Common pattern: brows down". Footer teaching note "These are grammatical cues, not simply emotions." and "Rhetorical questions and greetings can differ. Read the whole context." No made-up lexical manual sign. Distinguish brows clearly, not merely eyes wider.

title: A vs S: WATCH THE THUMB
detail: Title "A vs S: WATCH THE THUMB"; subtitle "A small handshape difference you can see". Two oversized photorealistic RIGHT HANDS palm-side to camera, cropped at forearm on ivory background. Left labeled "A": four fingers curled fully into fist, thumb extended straight upright ALONG THE SIDE of fist next to index finger, thumb NOT across fingers. Right labeled "S": four fingers curled into same fist, thumb lies diagonally ACROSS THE FRONT of the curled fingers, thumb tip near middle finger, NOT hidden inside fist. Fingers closed not extended, no extra digits. Under each large image matching macro closeup of thumb placement with teal outline and arrow. Text "A: thumb beside the fist" / "S: thumb across the fingers". Bottom text "Handshape names are not whole-word translations." No words mapped to A or S.

title: SIT vs CHAIR
detail: Title "SIT vs CHAIR"; subtitle "The movement changes the word". Two stacked rows of closeup photoreal hands at chest level with small adult signer face above, neutral. Clear anatomical correct H handshapes on BOTH hands: index and middle fingers extended TOGETHER horizontally, ring and pinky curled, thumb folded. Nondominant left hand palm DOWN two fingers point to the signer's right. Dominant right hand index and middle fingers together point to signer's left and lie CROSSWISE on TOP of left extended fingers (perpendicular fingers, overlapping near fingers' middles). Show top-down-oblique view for clarity. Row1 "SIT": before above and after contact snapshot, ONE larger downward arrow labeled "One movement". Row2 "CHAIR": same handshape and contact arrangement, two small repeated tap arrows with dots numbered1 and2 labeled "Two small movements". Labels "Same basic hand arrangement" and "Watch the full motion in video." NO V-spread fingers, no fist, no upright index, no hand clasp. Make the precise crossed-two-finger handshape the main subject.

title: HOW ASL CARRIES INFORMATION
detail: Title "HOW ASL CARRIES INFORMATION"; subtitle "Look at hands, face, body and motion". Five horizontal color-coded rows with LARGE photoreal demonstrator images and modest text. Row1 "HANDSHAPE" shows closeups of SAME right hand: closed fist, spread open hand, curved C-shaped hand; label "How the hand is formed" (NO word mappings). Row2 "LOCATION" same woman open spread right hand with thumb by chin vs thumb by forehead, label "Where the sign is made" (no word labels). Row3 "MOVEMENT" same woman's upright flat hands palms facing each other at chest, a start and finish further apart with outward arrows; label "The path and repetition". Row4 "PALM ORIENTATION" same right flat hand palm-side toward camera vs back-of-hand toward camera; label "Which way the palm faces". Row5 "NONMANUAL CUES" same woman's face neutral vs raised brows vs lowered brows, label "Face, head and body also contribute". Bottom "The parameters work together in context." No claim one handshape equals one English word, no mini illegible text. Person photographs must dominate.
